The annotation registry. An annotation is written as Annotation id="<type>", with AnnotationType the type and AnnotationValue the value. Annotations are the first child of the code. An empty cell produces no annotation. Each annotation is written on one line of the XML, so grep -c counts them. The 0.3.0 message holds 22 codelists with 299 codes (eight of them sentinels), 32 GLOBAL_CODE annotations (27 filled global_urn cells plus five sentinels) and 11 SDMX_CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPT annotations. The annotation types in use are:

GLOBAL_CODE: the full code URN of the matching code in a global list (Section 3.8).
AFW_<COLUMN>: one per codelist column that has no SDMX slot, including AFW_STATUS, AFW_VERSION_ADDED, AFW_REPLACED_BY and AFW_NOTES.
AFW_SENTINEL: Y on a sentinel code added by the generator.
AFW_SOURCE_FILE and AFW_METADATA_VERSION: the repository path of the CSV an artefact was generated from, and the metadata version. Every maintainable carries AFW_METADATA_VERSION; AFW_SOURCE_FILE is left out where ARTEFACTS.csv has no source_file (the organisation schemes, the dataflow, the metadataflow and the two agreements). Maintainables carry no AFW_STATUS: the status column of ARTEFACTS.csv is not exported.
SDMX_CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPT: on a concept that matches an SDMX cross-domain concept (Section 3.5).

Special cases:

CL_GEO_SCHEME.csv is keyed by ref_area and code. Its SDMX code id is <ref_area>_<code>, for example SEN_ADM1, and the two parts are also kept as the annotations AFW_REF_AREA and AFW_CODE. The importer splits the id on the first underscore.
Sentinels (D42). The generator appends _T (“Total”) and _Z (“Not applicable”) as real codes, reading the DSD file’s sentinel column: _T to CL_GEO; _T and _Z to CL_SEX and CL_AGE; _T to CL_URBANISATION and CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN; _Z to CL_QUALIFIER. That is eight sentinel codes in all. Each carries AFW_SENTINEL = Y, which the importer uses to drop it again. Five of them also carry one GLOBAL_CODE, the matching code in the list’s own global counterpart: CL_SEX _T and _Z point to SDMX:CL_SEX(2.1)._T and ._Z; CL_AGE._T points to IAEG-SDGs:CL_AGE(1.25)._T, CL_URBANISATION._T to IAEG-SDGs:CL_URBANISATION(1.10)._T, and CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN._T to IAEG-SDGs:CL_QUANTILE(1.1)._T. All of these are written as full code URNs. The other three, CL_AGE._Z, CL_GEO._T and CL_QUALIFIER._Z, have no matching code in their own list’s global counterpart and carry no GLOBAL_CODE. The sentinels still never appear in the codelist CSVs (Section 6.1).
Full URNs. GLOBAL_CODE and global_urn values are always full code URNs, urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.codelist.Code=<agency>:<id>(<version>).<code>, never the short form.
Derived codelists (D43). Three registries become codelists. CL_SOURCE comes from registries/SOURCES.csv, named by source_id, described by notes. CL_SURVEY comes from surveys/SURVEYS.csv, named by survey_name. CL_FIGURE comes from registries/FIGURES.csv, named by title_en. CL_SOURCE and CL_SURVEY codes carry only id, name, description and AFW_STATUS; CL_FIGURE codes carry id and name only, with no AFW_STATUS. Every other column goes to a metadataset (Section 3.6). With the 19 codelists generated from the codelist CSVs, that makes 22 codelists, among 32 artefacts in all. This gives SOURCE_ID a real codelist. SERIES_PLAN.csv derives no codelist: series ids contain ., which the SDMX IDType for code ids forbids, so SERIES_ID stays an uncoded String whose values the validator checks against SERIES_PLAN.csv (Section 6.1).
Names and descriptions of artefacts come from metadata/structure/ARTEFACTS.csv (D44). It lists every SDMX artefact to generate, one row each, with artefact_id, artefact_type (the SDMX class name), agency_id, source_file, name_en, description_en, status, version_added and notes. The generator iterates over it, so the list of what to generate is data, not code.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
3.5 Concepts
The concept scheme CS_AFW360 has one concept per component id of Table 7, from FREQ to OBS_COMMENT. The five COMP_BREAKDOWN_n and the five MEASURE_QUAL_n are separate concepts. It also has one concept per metadata attribute of the MSD (Section 3.6).

A component’s concept takes its name and description from the DSD file (name_en, description). A metadata attribute’s concept takes them from COLUMNS.csv: the column humanised as the name, and description as the description.
The scheme holds 82 concepts: 34 for the components and 48 for the metadata attributes. Concept ids are shared between the DSD and the MSD: REF_AREA, TIME_PERIOD and NOTES recur and are defined once (the first definition wins, DSD components first), and SOURCE is both a parent of the MSD and the concept of the FIGURES.csv column source. The four parent concepts SURVEY, SOURCE, TEXT and FIGURE have no rows in COLUMNS.csv, so the generator gives them a fixed name and description and no core representation.
A concept that matches an SDMX cross-domain concept carries the annotation SDMX_CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPT, whose value is the full concept URN in SDMX:CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPTS(2.0), for example urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.conceptscheme.Concept=SDMX:CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPTS(2.0).FREQ (the same full-URN rule as GLOBAL_CODE). All eleven targets exist in that scheme (checked against a copy fetched once): FREQ, REF_AREA, TIME_PERIOD, OBS_VALUE, OBS_STATUS, UNIT_MEASURE, SEX, AGE, INDICATOR, OBS_COMMENT (to COMMENT) and SOURCE_ID (to DATA_SOURCE).
Core representation: a coded concept references its codelist; a numeric one carries the TextFormat of Table 7; a text one is String. SERIES_ID is not coded, so its concept is String (Section 6.1). TIME_PERIOD carries TextFormat textType="GregorianYear", the same as its time-dimension local representation.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
3.6 Reference metadata
Documentary metadata goes where SDMX puts it: in metadatasets of a metadata structure (D43).

MSD WB.AFW360:MSD_AFW360(0.3.0) has four presentational parent attributes, SURVEY, SOURCE, TEXT and FIGURE. Each parent is isPresentational="true", minOccurs="0", maxOccurs="1", with no LocalRepresentation, because the XSD default for minOccurs is 1 and each metadataset fills only one parent. Each parent has one child per source column, minus the id and status columns, with ids equal to the column names upper-cased. Children have TextFormat textType="String", minOccurs="0" and maxOccurs="1".

SURVEY: 23 children from SURVEYS.csv (REF_AREA, TIME_PERIOD, SURVEY_NAME, … NOTES).
SOURCE: 12 children from SOURCES.csv (every column except source_id and status, so NOTES is included).
TEXT: 7 children from content/TEXT.csv: SLOT, REF_AREA, TIME_PERIOD, ORDER, TITLE, BODY, UPDATED_ON. BODY holds the Markdown source: the body cell, or the content of the file named in file (relative to content/text/, CRLF changed to LF, trailing newline kept); file wins over body, and file itself has no child.
FIGURE: 15 children from FIGURES.csv (REF_AREA … NOTES, excluding figure_id and status).

That is 57 children and 61 MetadataAttribute elements in all. Each child’s concept is the CS_AFW360 concept of the same id. Child ids repeat across parents (REF_AREA and TIME_PERIOD under SURVEY, TEXT and FIGURE; FIGURE.SOURCE shares its id with the parent SOURCE), which the XSD allows because ids need only be unique among siblings. The shared REF_AREA and TIME_PERIOD concepts keep their coded or GregorianYear core representation; the MSD overrides it locally with String.
Metadataflow MDF_AFW360 has the structure MSD_AFW360 and four explicit Target elements, one per targeted artefact: the codelists CL_SURVEY, CL_SOURCE and CL_FIGURE, and the dataflow AFW360_HH, each as a full URN with version 0.3.0. Wildcard targets are schema-valid but not used. The generator rewrites the versions at each release, like every other reference.
Metadatasets, one per registry row, are written as SDMX-CSV 2.1 metadata messages under sdmx/metadata/. The header is MDSTRUCTURE,MDSTRUCTURE_ID,METADATASET_ID,TARGET_TYPES,TARGET_IDS, then the attribute columns. MDSTRUCTURE is metadataflow and MDSTRUCTURE_ID is WB.AFW360:MDF_AFW360(0.3.0). Presentational parents have no column; each child appears as <PARENT>.<CHILD>, for example SURVEY.SURVEY_NAME. Metadatasets are not versioned.
Targets are whole artefacts, as the SDMX-CSV 2.1 metadata guide defines them: TARGET_TYPES is a REST structure resource name and TARGET_IDS is AGENCY:ID(VERSION). The guide has no form that targets a single code. The item a metadataset describes is identified by its METADATASET_ID and by the key attributes inside it, such as SURVEY.REF_AREA and SURVEY.TIME_PERIOD. TEXT.csv rows are metadatasets about a country; they target the dataflow and name the country in TEXT.REF_AREA.

pysdmx 1.20.0 has no SDMX-CSV metadata reader (Format.REFMETA_SDMX_CSV_2_1_0 exists, but no reader uses it), so the independent check of these files is a header check in tools/verify/verify_sdmx.py. That check is weaker than the rules above: it matches each header cell against the MSD attribute ids by the last dotted segment only, and it does not check MDSTRUCTURE_ID, TARGET_TYPES or the uniqueness of METADATASET_ID. The project validator’s SDMX.STALE check covers those rules, because it regenerates the files and compares them byte for byte. FMR does not read them either: its SDMX-ML 3.0 profile has no MSD (Section 3.11).

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
3.7 Providers

DataProviderScheme DATA_PROVIDERS (agency WB.AFW360, fixed version) has one provider, AFW_POV (“AFW DIP/POV team”). The ProvisionAgreement PA_AFW360_HH links the dataflow and the provider.
MetadataProviderScheme METADATA_PROVIDERS (agency WB.AFW360) has the provider AFW_POV. The MetadataProvisionAgreement MPA_AFW360 links the metadataflow and the provider.
The agreements reference DATA_PROVIDERS(1.0) and METADATA_PROVIDERS(1.0), the fixed versions the XSD patterns require. The SDMX.URN check exempts these references (Section 3.1). Both agreements are cheap and let FMR validate data under a provision agreement later.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
3.9 What stays outside SDMX
Project-only metadata stays CSV and is documented as tooling metadata outside SDMX (D45): TAB_PLAN.csv, SERIES_PLAN.csv, RULES.csv, INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv, QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv, the LEGACY_* files, COLUMNS.csv, DSD_AFW360_HH.csv itself and the manifests. Required coverage and arithmetic rules could be written in SDMX (a DataConstraint for allowed content, VTL for rules), but neither is used in this release: the project validator keeps that job. A DataConstraint for allowed content is a later option.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
3.10 The generated sdmx/ folder
pipeline/build_sdmx.R reads metadata/ and content/ and writes sdmx/:
sdmx/
  README.md                            what is here, how it is generated, how to load it into FMR
  structures/AFW360_structures.xml     one SDMX-ML 3.1 structure message with every artefact
  metadata/MDS_SURVEYS.csv             SDMX-CSV 2.1 metadata messages (D43)
  metadata/MDS_SOURCES.csv
  metadata/MDS_TEXT.csv
  metadata/MDS_FIGURES.csv
Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root .           # rewrite sdmx/
Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root . --check   # exit 1 if any file under sdmx/ is stale
Staleness rule. The files under sdmx/ are committed with the metadata that produced them. The output is deterministic: the message header has the fixed id AFW360_STRUCTURES, the sender WB_AFW360 and a prepared timestamp (--timestamp, default 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z), so the same CSVs always give the same bytes. --check regenerates into a temporary folder, compares bytes and prints one line per file (five lines). The repository has no CI: whoever changes metadata/ or content/ runs build_sdmx.R --check (or validate.R, whose SDMX.STALE check does the same) before committing, and a reviewer reruns it on the pull request, in the same way as for a stale table of this document (D28, D20). Outputs built with a custom --timestamp are reported stale. Nobody edits sdmx/ by hand.
The validator’s SDMX module (pipeline/R/validate_sdmx.R, Section 12) holds six checks:

SDMX.STALE (ERROR): regenerates the structure message and the four MDS_*.csv files with the default timestamp into a temporary folder and compares every file under sdmx/ except *.md; a differing, missing or unexpected file is a finding.
SDMX.XSD (ERROR): the message is valid against the SDMX-ML 3.1 XSDs vendored in pipeline/xsd/sdmx-ml-3.1/; one finding per libxml2 error.
SDMX.URN (ERROR): every urn:sdmx: reference outside annotations resolves to a maintainable, or a direct-child item of one, in the same message; every Parent exists; a sub-agency A.B is declared as agency B in a scheme of A; and every reference from a semver artefact points at a semver artefact, except the (1.0) organisation schemes and their items. Component-level URNs do not occur today and would be reported unresolved.
SDMX.IDENT (ERROR): every maintainable has agencyID WB.AFW360 (WB for AGENCIES), a version equal to metadata/VERSION (absent on the three fixed-version schemes), an id valid for the XSD IDType, and a non-empty English name.
SDMX.CSV_HEADER (ERROR): each data file’s header equals the 37 data columns, and every STRUCTURE_ID is WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(<VERSION>).
SDMX.SKIPPED (INFO): reported once when the root has no sdmx/ folder, like DOCS.SKIPPED; SDMX.XSD, SDMX.URN and SDMX.IDENT then report nothing.

Every validator run sources the SDMX writers, regenerates the outputs and validates them against the XSD, which adds a few seconds; a copy of the repository used as --root therefore needs pipeline/R and content/. The message is parsed from its bytes, not its path (libxml2 on Windows kept the file locked after a failed parse).
Verification tools outside the pipeline. tools/verify/ is an independent reader in Python (pysdmx 1.20.0, venv under tools/verify/.venv), used by reviewers and never by the pipeline (D30):

verify_sdmx.py --root . reads the structure message and prints the maintainables by class (32 artefacts), reads each data file as SDMX-CSV 2.1 and prints its observation count (3003 for SEN, 2268 for GNB), header-checks the four metadata messages, and exits 1 on any failure. pysdmx 1.20.0 cannot read com:AnnotationValue, which the XSD allows and this project uses, so the tool validates the original bytes against the schema and hands pysdmx a copy without annotation values. It calls the SDMX-CSV 2.1 reader directly, because read_sdmx sniffs the format and gives a generic error on a bad header. read_sdmx(validate=True) validates against pysdmx’s bundled schemas, not pipeline/xsd/.
xsd_validate.py <xsd> <xml> validates with lxml against the vendored XSDs and prints valid or the first error.
check_urns.py <xml> resolves every WB.AFW360 URN inside the message and prints unresolved: <n>; a maintainable without a version attribute (the organisation schemes) is registered under version 1.0, items included.

pipeline/reconcile.R checks every cell of the data files against the legacy workbooks. It keeps private copies of the few io.R helpers it needs, so it stays independent of the pipeline’s reader, and still sources codes.R for slot filling. The projection test in pipeline/tests/testthat/ (test-projection-*.R) maps each new data file back onto the 31 columns of the previous layout and compares it with the committed old file; the only allowed differences are the removed DATAFLOW column and NaN against empty on the O rows.
pipeline/import_sdmx.R does the reverse of the generator: it reads an SDMX-ML 3.0 or 3.1 structure message and shows (--diff) or writes (--apply) the changes to the CSVs under metadata/. --apply rewrites all 20 target files (19 codelist CSVs and ARTEFACTS.csv), changed or not. What flows back is listed in Section 3.11.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
3.11 Editing and validating with FMR
The Fusion Metadata Registry (FMR) can load the structure message, validate data files against it, and edit artefacts. It is optional: everything is published as plain files in the repository, and no live registry or REST service is run for the dashboard (D36). FMR is installed (D35), without Docker: FMR 12.4.2 as the WAR of Apache Tomcat 10.1.60, on Java 21 (Azul Zulu 21.0.12.1), with a portable MySQL 8.0 database, all under the gitignored tools/fmr/runtime/. The exact install, start and stop steps are in fmr-guide.qmd; the scripts are in tools/fmr/.
FMR 12.4.2 does not read SDMX-ML 3.1. Loading sdmx/structures/AFW360_structures.xml returns HTTP 400 with FMR error 150, “Unrecognised file format”. The generator therefore has a second output profile: Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root . --out-root <dir> --sdmx-ml-version 3.0 writes the same artefacts with the SDMX-ML 3.0 namespaces, without the MSD, the metadataflow and the metadata provision agreement (whose 3.0 XML differs). It writes only the structure message and only under an --out-root other than the root, and refuses --check. The 3.1 file stays the canonical committed output; the 3.0 profile is written to tmp/ for loading. The data files need no change: FMR accepts the SDMX-CSV 2.1 files as they are (it labels them “SDMX CSV v2.0”) and validates them without error.
The agency WB must exist first. FMR resolves WB:AGENCIES(1.0) against its own SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0) scheme, so the top-level agency WB has to be registered there before the project’s structures load (otherwise HTTP 404, error 100, “Could not resolve reference”). tools/fmr/fmr_load.R does this once, idempotently, by posting tools/fmr/agencies_bootstrap.xml.
The workflow is:

Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root . generates sdmx/.
Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_load.R --root . checks that FMR answers, registers WB when missing, builds the 3.0 profile into tmp/fmr/v30/ and loads it (action REPLACE, so a reload is harmless).
Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_validate.R --root . posts each data file to /ws/public/data/validate and saves the report as tmp/fmr/<ISO3>_<YEAR>_<ESTIMATION>_validation.json. A clean report has "Errors":false; that field is the test, not the absence of the word “error”. Steps 1 to 3 are all that validation-only use needs.
To edit, work in FMR on a copy versioned <next>-draft, then export with Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_export.R --root . --out tmp/fmr/export.xml. FMR exports SDMX-ML 3.0 only (a request for 3.1 returns HTTP 406) and rewrites the message header. Run Rscript pipeline/import_sdmx.R --root . --diff tmp/fmr/export.xml to see the changes against the CSVs, then --apply, and commit through a pull request. At release, bump VERSION, regenerate sdmx/ and reload (Section 11).

What flows back from FMR. An unedited export round-trips with no change (299 codes, 2371 annotations, 399 descriptions). The importer brings back codes, names, descriptions, parents and annotations of the 19 CSV codelists, and the names and descriptions of the other artefacts in ARTEFACTS.csv. It does not bring back: the ARTEFACTS.csv columns status, version_added, notes, agency_id and source_file; edits to the derived codelists CL_SOURCE, CL_SURVEY and CL_FIGURE (reported, never written; edit their registries instead); AFW_METADATA_VERSION; the structure of the concept scheme, DSD, MSD, dataflow and agreements; non-English names; sentinel names and their GLOBAL_CODE, which are dropped with the sentinel. The MSD, metadataflow and metadata provision agreement are not in the 3.0 profile at all. A code added in FMR to a codelist whose CSV has no COLUMNS.csv rows stops the import. The importer reads SDMX-ML 3.0 and 3.1 alike and falls back to AnnotationTitle when AnnotationValue is absent. FMR’s submit and error responses are always SDMX-ML 2.1.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
section: 4.2 Every breakdown variable carries a universe
text:
4.2 Every breakdown variable carries a universe
CL_BRK_VAR.universe names the population that the categories partition. This is what makes each of POP_SH, POP_HH_SH and POP_HE_SH work as a single indicator for its stat_unit: the share is the category’s weighted count divided by the universe’s, and the row’s N_POP is the universe’s (Section 2.6). “Share of employed in agriculture” (individuals, POP_SH) and “share of households with two enterprises” (households, POP_HH_SH) use the same mechanism but different codes, because they count different units (D4).
A recall period that defines who belongs to a group — “employed in the last 12 months” versus “employed right now” — is a property of that group’s universe, not of the share indicator. It is recorded in CL_BRK_VAR.universe and the category’s definition_en, never by giving the indicator a different ref_period. POP_SH, POP_HH_SH and POP_HE_SH all carry ref_period = INTERVIEW, whatever recall period their breakdown’s universe uses.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
section: 4.3 Worked example: adding sector of employment
text:
4.3 Worked example: adding sector of employment

Decide whose characteristic it is. “Sector of an individual’s main job” (EMP_SECTOR, describes IND) and “sector of the household head’s main job” (HHH_SECTOR, describes HHH) are two different variables. The first can break down only individual-level indicators; the second can break down household indicators such as the poverty rate.
Register it in CL_BRK_VAR: describes = IND, applies_to_units = IND, universe = employed persons aged 15–64, classification = ISIC Rev.4, partition = Y, slot_order = 60.
Register the categories in CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN: EMP_SECTOR_AGR for ISIC section A, EMP_SECTOR_IND for B–F and EMP_SECTOR_SER for G–U.
Add a cut to TAB_PLAN.
Produce the rows. When the cut is crossed with individual sex, the rows for women also carry SEX=F. When it is crossed with quintile, QUINT has the lower slot_order, so it takes slot 1 and EMP_SECTOR takes slot 2.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
6.1 Code rules

Uppercase ASCII letters, digits and _; start with a letter; at most 32 characters, the Stata variable-name limit. P-codes are used as issued and already comply.
_T and _Z are reserved sentinels and never appear as codes in a codelist CSV. The SDMX generator adds them as real codes, “Total” and “Not applicable”, to every codelist whose dimension admits them, as the sentinel column of DSD_AFW360_HH.csv says, each with the annotation AFW_SENTINEL = Y. The importer strips them again (D42, Section 3.4).
A code never changes meaning, and is never reused or deleted. A changed definition means a new code, with the old one DEPRECATED and replaced_by filled. Rewording a label is free.
Breakdown and qualifier categories are <var_code>_<category>. The whole code must still fit in 32 characters, so keep var_code short.
Indicator codes are <THEME>_<SUBJECT>[_<DETAIL>] and contain no poverty line, PPP round, welfare concept, COICOP division, unit or breakdown, because all of those are dimensions. Use POV_HC, never POV_HC_PL420.
Series ids are the indicator code, then its qualifier categories in slot order, then its defining category, joined by .: POV_HC.POVLINE_PL420.PPP_2021, CONS_SH.COICOP_CP01, POP_SH.EMP_SECTOR_AGR. Series ids are the only ids that contain a dot, and are therefore not SDMX code ids (see below). A series id is immutable once the series is ACTIVE (D13).
Source ids follow the code rules and are unique in SOURCES.csv, with one exception: they end in a run-version suffix _v<N>, whose lowercase v is the only lowercase letter allowed in any code. The recommended pattern is <ISO3>_<SURVEY>_<PROGRAM>_v<N>, for example SEN_EHCVM2021_LEGACY_v1.
In Stata, name the variable holding an indicator after its code in lower case, so no lookup table is needed.
Codes are also SDMX ids. Every code becomes an SDMX code id, which may hold only letters, digits, _, -, @ and $. The rules above are stricter, except for series ids. Series ids may contain ., which the SDMX IDType pattern for code ids forbids, so they are not SDMX code ids: SERIES_ID is an uncoded String attribute, and no codelist is derived from SERIES_PLAN.csv (D43). Artefact ids such as CL_SEX or DSD_AFW360_HH are NCNames: a letter, then letters, digits, _ or - (Section 3.1).
Codes follow global lists where one exists (D32). A code that matches a global code keeps or takes that code’s value where these rules allow, and records the global code’s full URN in global_urn (Section 3.8).

6.4 CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN.csv
Extra columns: var_code (R), parent (O, a category of the same variable, for nested classifications), order (R, display order). definition_en is required wherever the boundary is not obvious, such as age cutoffs, ISIC groupings and quantile ranking rules.
A category’s variable is always looked up through this var_code column, never inferred by parsing the code’s prefix: HE_ is a prefix of HE_COUNT_0, but that does not make it a category of a variable called HE.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
6.5 CL_QUAL_VAR.csv and CL_QUALIFIER.csv
CL_QUAL_VAR extra columns: slot_order (R), requires (C, other qualifier variables that must appear with it, such as PPP for POVLINE), owner (R).
CL_QUALIFIER extra columns: var_code (R), value (C, the numeric parameter, such as 3.00 for POVLINE_PL300), basis (C, what that value is expressed in), order (R).
Which categories of one qualifier variable may appear with which categories of another is not a column of either codelist; it is a row of QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv (Section 6.14, D18). When a category’s allowed set for some qualifier variable is _Z — as POVLINE_NPL’s is for PPP — that overrides the variable-level requires: a national-line row does not also require a PPP round, even though POVLINE otherwise requires PPP.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
6.6 CL_GEO_SCHEME.csv and CL_GEO.csv
Schemes are parallel, not nested. ADM1 regions, ADM2 départements, Senegal’s zones and Guinea-Bissau’s agro-ecological zones are four different ways of cutting a country, and each is stored as its own set of units. Even where one scheme happens to group the units of another, as Senegal’s zones group its regions, nothing is derived from that nesting, and no scheme is required to decompose into another.
CL_GEO_SCHEME has one row per country and scheme, keyed ref_area + code (Table 16). has_geometry is Y only for ADM0 and ADM1 (Section 9.1). nests_in names another scheme only where nesting is genuine, for optional roll-up checks, never to derive geometry.

Extra columns: iso2 (R, the P-code prefix), currency (R, ISO 4217), wb_region (R).
Currency matters more than it seems. “FCFA” is two different currencies: XOF (CFA franc BCEAO, used in WAEMU, including SEN and GNB) and XAF (CFA franc BEAC). Eight AFW economies use neither. text:
6.10 Manifest
AFW360_HH_<ISO3>_<YEAR>_<ESTIMATION>_manifest.csv has two columns, key and value. The 17 keys are, in this order:
structure_id (WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0); equals every row’s STRUCTURE_ID), sdmx_csv_version (2.1.0), dsd_version, metadata_version, ref_area, time_period, estimation (CL_ESTIMATION; equals every row’s ESTIMATION), survey_id (the base survey, also for a model-based file), sources (the SOURCE_ID values that appear in the file, space-separated), file_name, n_rows, producer, program, software, run_timestamp (ISO 8601), status (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, VALIDATED, PUBLISHED), notes.
The manifest summarises the file; it holds nothing that a row needs. Precision is on each row (PRECISION), and the program run that produced each row is its SOURCE_ID, whose registry row carries the program version and inputs (Section 6.15). The source_type and precision keys of version 0.1.0 are gone (D15, D16, D17).
dsd_version is not chosen independently: the DSD is versioned with the metadata package, so it equals metadata/VERSION.
In version 0.3.0 the key dataflow became structure_id, the SDMX short reference to the dataflow and its version, and sdmx_csv_version was added (D46). The other 15 keys are unchanged. The manifest is a project-level sidecar, not an SDMX artefact: it describes a file (D43, D45).
TIME_PERIOD is the year the estimate refers to, which is not always a survey year. A microsimulated 2026 poverty rate has TIME_PERIOD=2026, ESTIMATION=MODEL, a source whose survey_id is SEN_EHCVM_2021, and OBS_STATUS=E on every row (Section 2.3).

A series is one row: its series_id (Section 6.1), the INDICATOR, the qualifier categories in MEASURE_QUALS, and, for a share indicator, the category it is a share of in DEFINING_BREAKDOWN, for example EMP_SECTOR_AGR for the series “share of employed persons working in agriculture”.

Three columns were added in metadata version 0.2:

It is composed by default from the indicator’s short_name_en and the qualifier and category names, and a human overwrites it wherever the composed form reads badly. The dashboard shows name_en, never the id.
estimation lists the file kinds in which the series is expected: SURVEY, MODEL, or both space-separated (D17). Every series of version 0.1.0 has SURVEY.
status gains two values beyond DRAFT and ACTIVE (D23). On a row for a specific country, NOT_PRODUCED records that the country’s survey cannot support the series, and DEVIATES records that the country produces it under a definition that departs from the dictionary’s; both require notes. A country row overrides the ALL row for the same series_id (Section 2.7).

text:
6.13 Verification rules: RULES.csv
Every rule that the validator applies to values is a row of metadata/rules/RULES.csv (D18). Rules used to be space-separated tokens in a column of the indicator dictionary; as a table they can be versioned, given a severity and a tolerance, and attached to a series rather than an indicator, without touching the dictionary.



Table 23: Columns of RULES.csv










Column
Status
Description

Unique id of the rule: <scope_code or AFW360_HH>.<rule>[.<param>], e.g. POV_HC.MONOTONE_IN.POVLINE.

R
What the rule applies to: DATAFLOW (every row), INDICATOR (every series of one indicator) or SERIES (one series).


scope_code
C
The indicator code or series_id the rule applies to; empty when scope is DATAFLOW.


rule
R
The rule from the vocabulary: RANGE_0_1, RANGE_NONNEG, AGG_SUM, AGG_NPOP_MEAN, AGG_BRACKET, SUM_TO_1_OVER, SUM_TO_1_OVER_BRK, MONOTONE_IN, RELIABILITY_MIN_NOBS or RELIABILITY_MAX_CV.


param
C
The rule’s argument: the qualifier variable for SUM_TO_1_OVER and MONOTONE_IN, the threshold for the two RELIABILITY rules; empty otherwise.

O
Absolute tolerance that overrides the validator’s default, computed from each row’s PRECISION; empty to use the default.

R
ERROR (the file fails validation) or WARN (reported only).

R

A rule has a scope: DATAFLOW for a rule that applies to every row (scope_code empty), INDICATOR for every series of one indicator, or SERIES for one series. rule is one of the vocabulary below, param is its argument where it takes one, tolerance overrides the default absolute tolerance of Section 12 when filled, and severity is ERROR or WARN. The rule’s rule_id is <scope_code or AFW360_HH>.<rule>, followed by .<param> when the parameter is a qualifier variable; a numeric threshold is not part of the id, so AFW360_HH.RELIABILITY_MAX_CV keeps its id when the threshold changes.
Rule vocabulary:

RANGE_0_1, RANGE_NONNEG: bounds on OBS_VALUE.
AGG_SUM: over a population cut that is a partition, the children’s values sum to the parent’s.
AGG_NPOP_MEAN: the N_POP-weighted average of the children equals the parent.
AGG_BRACKET: the parent lies within the range spanned by its children; used where AGG_NPOP_MEAN cannot be computed, as in a legacy file with no N_POP.
SUM_TO_1_OVER, param a qualifier variable: the categories of that qualifier sum to 1, for example over COICOP.
SUM_TO_1_OVER_BRK: the categories of the series’ defining breakdown sum to 1.
MONOTONE_IN, param a qualifier variable: the value does not fall as that qualifier’s order rises, for example over POVLINE.
RELIABILITY_MIN_NOBS, RELIABILITY_MAX_CV, scope DATAFLOW, param the threshold: the two thresholds of the low-reliability rule (Section 2.6).

EQUALS_NPOP_RATIO of version 0.1.0 is retired: with N_POP defined as the denominator on a share row (D19), the category’s population is OBS_VALUE × N_POP by definition, so the rule checked nothing.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
7.1 Estimation rules

Code the indicator variable as missing for units outside its universe, so they leave both the numerator and the denominator.
Estimate with the survey design declared (weights, strata, PSUs), and use subpopulation estimation for groups rather than dropping observations, so that standard errors stay correct.
Use the weight named in the dictionary (POP = household weight × household size, for person-level statistics computed on household data).
Publish every estimate. Do not blank, round away or drop a small cell; report its N_OBS.
Write values unrounded, in base units.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
7.2 A note on legacy conversions
Files that the converter produces from the legacy Excel inherit values already rounded to two decimals, and they carry no sample sizes. Their source in SOURCES.csv has kind = LEGACY_CONVERSION, and every row carries PRECISION (0.01 × scale, the workbook’s two decimals taken to base units). The validator widens its tolerances by each row’s PRECISION and does not demand STD_ERR, CI_*, N_OBS or N_POP on rows of such a source. This exemption belongs to the source kind, never to new production.
A cell already known to be wrong is withheld, not converted: its row is absent from the file, not present with a value or a comment. The exclusion is registered in LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv (action WITHHOLD, with a reason and evidence) and subtracted from the required rows (Section 2.7, D5). Action COMMENT is different: the value is kept and OBS_COMMENT records why it is suspicious but worth keeping.
OBS_STATUS=O means “no value available” generally, not only “in the universe but no observations fell in this cell” (D9). On a row whose source is a legacy conversion, every O requires an OBS_COMMENT prefixed LEGACY_EMPTY:, explaining why the legacy sheet has no value for that cell.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
7.3 How the dashboard shows reliability
Since nothing is suppressed, the dashboard carries the burden of honesty:

Every value is shown with its N_OBS, available on hover, in a details panel or in the downloaded table.
Charts show the confidence interval where one exists.
A cell flagged OBS_STATUS=U is visually de-emphasized rather than hidden, and the flag is set by the data, not by the dashboard (Section 2.6). OBS_STATUS=O renders as “no observations”, never as zero.
Displayed decimals are capped by the row’s PRECISION: a value converted from a workbook rounded to two decimals never shows more than those two accurate decimals in its display unit, however many CL_INDICATOR.decimals asks for elsewhere. This is the rule the dashboard must follow; the loader formats by display_as and decimals today, and capping by PRECISION is a later step.
Labels and formats come from the metadata, so that no chart, table or sentence composes a label or picks a format on its own: load_indicator_meta() gives each indicator’s display_as, decimals, higher_is and short_name_en, and each row carries its SERIES_ID and UNIT_MEASURE.

The loader. The dashboard reads only through the Python package afw360/ (D37); no chunk of index.qmd reads data_raw/. load_data(iso3, year=None, estimation="SURVEY") reads one SDMX-CSV file, checks its STRUCTURE_ID against metadata/VERSION, drops the three fixed columns and parses NaN; with year=None it takes the latest year’s file, it does not concatenate years. series(df, series_id, **dims) selects rows by exact equality and has no _T defaults: a single national value needs every breakdown dimension pinned to _T (GEO, SEX, AGE, URBANISATION, COMP_BREAKDOWN_1 to _5), otherwise it returns one row per value of the unpinned dimensions. load_text(iso3, slot) reads content/TEXT.csv, whose file column is relative to content/text/; load_figures(iso3) reads metadata/registries/FIGURES.csv, whose file column is relative to assets/figures/. load_boundaries(iso3, layer) reads the country’s GeoPackage (layers adm0 and adm1; file names differ in case, SEN_CODAB_v02.gpkg and GNB_CODAB_V01.gpkg) and renames its code column geo_code to GEO. Zone schemes are not yet named alike: the agro-ecological zones are scheme ZONES in Senegal and AEZ in Guinea-Bissau, and the dashboard accepts both. The deployment pins in the root requirements.txt include the Jupyter kernel packages (ipykernel, nbformat, nbclient), pyyaml and jinja2, which the render needs.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
8.1 Add an indicator

Search CL_INDICATOR for the same concept. If it exists, reuse it. Before creating a code, check whether the difference is a qualifier: a different poverty line, PPP round, welfare concept or COICOP division is never a new indicator. Neither is a population share; that is POP_SH, POP_HH_SH or POP_HE_SH with a breakdown, chosen by what the breakdown counts (D4).
If a near-duplicate exists, fill related and related_note on both rows.
Standardize the variables it needs in the harmonized microdata, so that the indicator is a plain aggregate of them (Section 1.4). Record them in source_questionnaire and source_vars, and the program that computes the indicator in program.
Fill every R column and the C columns that apply.
Register the qualifier variables it takes in INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv, the rules its values must satisfy in RULES.csv, and each of its series in SERIES_PLAN.csv with a display name.
Produce it for every applicable cut.
Open a pull request (Section 11).

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
8.2 Add a breakdown variable
Follow Section 4.3: decide describes and applies_to_units, write the universe, reuse an international classification if one exists, set slot_order, register the categories, and add the cuts. Expect small N_OBS in fine groups, and publish them anyway with their sample sizes.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
8.3 Add a qualifier variable

Confirm it is a qualifier: the population behind each category is the same one (Section 1.1).
Register it with a slot_order and, if it depends on another qualifier, requires.
Register its categories, with value and basis where they apply, and their pairings with other qualifier variables in QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv.
Add a row to INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv for every indicator that takes it, naming the allowed categories, and the new series to SERIES_PLAN.csv.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
8.4 Add a country
Follow the order in Section 1.4: metadata first, data last.

CL_AREA: add the country, with its ISO2 code (the P-code prefix) and its currency.
CL_GEO_SCHEME: register every spatial scheme the country will publish, with the local name of each level.
CL_GEO: register the units of each scheme, using the P-codes of the boundary file you will map with.
Indicators: check each indicator in CL_INDICATOR against the country’s survey, and reuse the code wherever the definition holds. Where it does not, register a new code linked to the old one through related and related_note (Section 8.1). Never stretch an existing definition to fit.
Breakdowns and qualifiers: map the survey’s own variable values to the shared codes, in the producer’s program. A country-specific category becomes a child of a shared code (a secondary-city stratum is parent = U), never an unrelated new code.
SURVEYS: add each survey round, with its design, welfare aggregate and national poverty line.
Boundaries: add the ADM0 and ADM1 boundary file and its GEO_SOURCES row (Section 9.4).
TAB_PLAN: add rows only where the country’s cuts differ from the shared ALL rows, for example for its own zone scheme.
SERIES_PLAN: add a country row for every series the survey cannot support (NOT_PRODUCED) or supports only under a different definition (DEVIATES), with the reason in notes.
Data: register the program run in SOURCES.csv, produce the data file and manifest for each reference year (Section 7), run the validator, and open one pull request with the metadata and the data together (Section 11).

Every other code comes from the shared codelists.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
section: 9.1 Maps exist for countries and ADM1 only
text:
9.1 Maps exist for countries and ADM1 only
has_geometry = Y is set for ADM0 and ADM1. Every other scheme, including ADM2, zones and agro-ecological zones, is published as tables with no map, no geometry file and no missing-geometry error. Neither Senegal’s zones nor Guinea-Bissau’s agro-ecological zones therefore need polygons.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
9.2 Storage
Boundaries are stored as GeoPackage (.gpkg) files, one per country per boundary vintage, with one layer per level:
geo/boundaries/SEN_CODAB_v02.gpkg     layers: adm0, adm1
Why not shapefiles: a shapefile is 5–6 files that must travel together. Its DBF field names are cut at 10 characters (the current files show cod_versio and adm1_ref_n), its text fields stop at 254 characters, its encoding is declared in a side-car .cpg, and its .prj carries no authority code (the current files say GCS_WGS_1984 with no EPSG number). A GeoPackage is one SQLite file with UTF-8 text, long field names, several layers and an SRS with its authority code, and geopandas, QGIS, ArcGIS and R all read it.
Rules:

Required layer fields: geo_code (matching CL_GEO.code), ref_area, scheme. A name column may be kept for convenience, but CL_GEO is authoritative, and disagreement is a warning, not an error.
CRS: EPSG:4326 in storage. Reproject only for display or area computation.
Hygiene: valid geometries, one feature per code, units covering the country exactly once. Geometry is built and checked with GEOS (sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)), invalid rings repaired with st_make_valid(), from the plain (non-_em) shapefiles as the source — SN01 and SN13 fail s2/GEOS validity as issued.
Vintages are explicit. valid_from and valid_to in CL_GEO describe the boundary release a code belongs to, not the period the data cover. SEN’s COD-AB v02 dates from 2024 while the data are for 2021, and that is not an error.
Derived layers are generated, never hand-edited. Simplified display copies are planned for geo/derived/, which does not exist yet; once built, they may be rebuilt at any time, and the simplification tolerance is kept in the build script.
Size: keep files in git while they are small. Beyond a few MB, use Git LFS or an external store, with the URL and checksum in the registry.

GEO_SOURCES.csv columns: source_id, ref_area, provider, version, valid_on, url, download_date, licence, attribution (the credit line the map must show), crs, file, layers, sha256, status, version_added, notes.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
9.3 Figures
Figures live at assets/figures/<ISO3>/<figure_id>.<ext> and are registered in FIGURES.csv, with columns figure_id, ref_area, time_period, theme, title_en, caption_en, alt_text_en (required: what a screen reader announces), indicators, source, producer, program, licence, file, sha256, status, version_added, notes.
Prefer generating figures from the data; an image is a last resort. Use SVG or PDF for charts, and PNG at twice display size for anything raster. The dashboard asks for a figure_id, not a file name.

text:
10.2 Live numbers in prose
Numbers typed into prose go stale, and nothing checks them; the current key messages are typed into index.qmd by hand. Instead, reference the data inline, as in Listing 2.



Listing 2: Live numbers in dashboard prose


Poverty at $4.20 a day stands at {{POV_HC:PL420}}, and {{POV_NUM:PL420}} million people are poor.
Rural poverty stands at {{POV_HC:PL420@URBANISATION=R}}.




The country and year come from the TEXT.csv row, and every breakdown defaults to the national total, so a plain {INDICATOR:QUALIFIER} is usually enough.
Anything else is added after @ as DIMENSION=CODE, separated by commas.
The dashboard formats each number with its indicator’s display_as and decimals (37.0% for a share, 6.52 for a count shown in millions), so prose and tables cannot disagree. Write only the words around the number.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
10.3 What this replaces
TEXT.csv replaces About_<ISO3>.txt, Messages_<ISO3>.txt and every string hardcoded in index.qmd. Figure captions stay with their images in FIGURES.csv.
State after the switch-over: the dashboard shows the About text (the old page offered only a download button). Message titles in TEXT.csv are not shown yet, because #| title: is ignored by the html format. Guinea-Bissau’s messages and About text are TBD and it has no FIGURES.csv row, so its page shows “TBD” and a “no figure” note until the content is written. Three CL_GEO names (SN_ZONES06, GW_AEZ01, GW_AEZ03) still carry “(TBD: legacy header truncated …)”; the charts cut the name at ” (TBD”. The legacy column label “29+” is mapped to HHH_AGE_GE35 (35 and over) and the label kept, pending the data lead’s confirmation.
For Senegal, About_SEN.txt becomes content/text/SEN/about.md; Messages_SEN.txt is stripped of its dashboard chunk wrappers and raw HTML and stored as DRAFT literal prose, with no number invented that is not already in the data, and both the file’s own message titles and index.qmd’s hardcoded ones recorded, the index.qmd version as the DRAFT candidate. About.txt is treated as Senegal-specific (ref_area = SEN), not shared boilerplate, despite being byte-identical to About_SEN.txt today. Messages_SEN.txt2 and Tables_SEN_TEST.xlsx are scratch files and are ignored.

10.4 Extending
Add or edit a row in TEXT.csv, and add a .md file if the text is long. The same pull request rules apply as for codelists.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
11.1 Generated tables
Every table in this document that lists the contents of a metadata file is written by pipeline/build_docs.R to .docs/generated/<table-id>.md and included where it appears (D20). Each fragment holds one Markdown table with its caption and cross-reference id, so a reference such as Table 4 keeps working. The script reads only metadata/ and content/, so it can be run at any time:
Rscript pipeline/build_docs.R --root .           # rewrite the fragments
Rscript pipeline/build_docs.R --root . --check   # exit 1 if any fragment is stale
The fragments are committed with the metadata that produced them. A pull request that edits a codelist without regenerating them fails the validator’s documentation check (Section 12), so the standard and the metadata cannot drift apart. Conceptual tables, such as the two families, the compositions, the example rows and the decisions, are written by hand and are not covered.

text:
13.1 Decisions taken



Table 33: Design decisions taken









Decision
Choice




Breakdowns
Named GEO, URBANISATION, SEX, AGE, plus five generic slots


Qualifiers
Five generic slots. Poverty line, PPP round, welfare concept, COICOP division and fiscal instrument are all qualifiers.


Population shares
Three indicators — POP_SH (individuals), POP_HH_SH (households), POP_HE_SH (enterprises) — chosen by what the breakdown counts, with the group named by the breakdown


Suppression
None. Every estimate is published, with its sample size and confidence interval attached.


Geography
Parallel spatial schemes, not a hierarchy. Maps only for country outlines and ADM1.


Language
English only


Who extends codelists
Producers, through pull requests reviewed by the data team


Tooling
Producers deliver CSV. The metadata bootstrap, the converter and the validator are written in R; the dashboard stays Python/Quarto and reads the harmonized CSVs through one loader.


Estimation method
A key dimension, ESTIMATION (SURVEY, MODEL), with one file per country, year and method, so a nowcast and a survey estimate for the same year coexist (D17)


Series identity
SERIES_ID is an attribute of every row, validated against SERIES_PLAN, which carries the display name (D13)


Units and precision in the file
UNIT_MEASURE on every row, currency resolved per country; PRECISION on every row, empty when exact (D14, D15)


Provenance
SOURCE_ID on every row, resolved through SOURCES.csv, which carries program version and inputs; the manifest only summarises (D16)


Rules and relations
Tables, RULES.csv, INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv and QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv, not packed codelist cells (D18)


Counts on share rows
N_OBS and N_POP are the denominator; partition checks run over population cuts only (D19)


Reliability
OBS_STATUS=U by rule, fewer than 30 records or a CV above 0.30, written by the producer and recomputed by the validator; one status per row with precedence M O E D U A (D22)


Series a country cannot match
Country rows in SERIES_PLAN with NOT_PRODUCED or DEVIATES; deviating rows carry OBS_STATUS=D (D23)


Versioning
0.x is pre-release: structural changes are batched into minor releases until 1.0.0, declared at the first validated producer file (D24)


Documentation
Every table that lists a metadata file is generated from it and checked for staleness (D20)


SDMX version
SDMX 3.1 family: SDMX-CSV 2.1.0 for data and reference metadata, SDMX-ML 3.1.0 for structures, no SDMX-JSON (D27, D29)


Source of truth
The CSVs; SDMX-ML is generated into sdmx/, committed and checked for staleness (D28)


SDMX tooling
R writes and XSD-validates the XML; Python only in the dashboard loader and in tools/verify/, outside the pipeline (D30)


Agency
WB.AFW360, a sub-agency of WB, declared by a local WB:AGENCIES scheme until the World Bank registers it (D31)


Global code lists
Codes aligned to SDMX, IAEG-SDGs and World Bank lists by value or by a GLOBAL_CODE annotation; global lists are not referenced (D32)


Measures
Nine: OBS_VALUE, STD_ERR, CI_LOWER, CI_UPPER, N_OBS, N_POP, N_OBS_NUM, DEFF, DF (D33)


Frequency
FREQ is the first dimension, always A (D34)


Registry
FMR 12.4.2 installed without Docker (D35); it loads the SDMX-ML 3.0 profile, validates the SDMX-CSV 2.1 data and exports 3.0 (Section 3.11). No live registry or REST service for the dashboard; everything is plain files (D36)


Dashboard data access
One loader, afw360/, reads data/, metadata/, content/, geo/ and assets/; no chunk reads data_raw/ (D37)


Action
ACTION=R in every published file; no D rows (D38)


Missing values
OBS_VALUE is NaN when OBS_STATUS is O or M; optional cells empty; mandatory attributes never empty (D39)


Artefact versions
Every artefact carries metadata/VERSION; a released version is immutable; edits go through a -draft copy (D40)


CSV-to-SDMX mapping
By convention, with an AFW_<COLUMN> annotation for every column that has no SDMX slot (D41)


Sentinels in SDMX
_T and _Z added as codes by the generator, stripped by the importer, never in the CSVs (D42)


Registries in SDMX
The three derived codelists CL_SOURCE, CL_SURVEY, CL_FIGURE; SERIES_ID uncoded, checked against SERIES_PLAN; descriptive columns and TEXT.csv as metadatasets of MSD_AFW360 (D43)


Artefact list
metadata/structure/ARTEFACTS.csv lists every artefact to generate (D44)


Outside SDMX
Plans, rules, relations, legacy maps, COLUMNS.csv, the DSD CSV and manifests stay project CSV; no VTL, no DataConstraint (D45)


Column order
Fixed columns, dimensions, TIME_PERIOD, measures, attributes: 37 columns, 19-column key (D46)

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
13.2 Open decisions

Age cutoff for household heads. The current Youth_HH / Older_HH boundary is undocumented; confirm it before publishing any HHH_AGE_* code.
Quintile definition. National or within-area ranking, person- or household-weighted. The answer goes in CL_BRK_VAR.definition_en.
Governance. Who owns metadata/ and reviews pull requests.
GNB survey metadata — closed by D6. EHCVM 2021/22 maps to TIME_PERIOD 2021, survey_id GNB_EHCVM_2021 (user-confirmed; About_GNB.txt remains a placeholder with no real survey metadata).
Where large binaries live. Git, Git LFS, or an external store referenced from GEO_SOURCES.csv.
Boundary vintage policy. Who decides when to adopt a new COD-AB release, given that P-codes can change and older data must still resolve.
Where variable-level metadata lives. Section 1.4 asks for documentation of every harmonized microdata variable behind an indicator. CL_INDICATOR names those variables but has nowhere to describe them. A variable dictionary per survey, kept with the producer programs or under metadata/, is the obvious candidate.
A country that cannot produce an indicator — closed by D23. A country row in SERIES_PLAN.csv with status = NOT_PRODUCED removes the series from that country’s required rows; DEVIATES keeps the rows and marks them OBS_STATUS=D (Section 6.12).
The Departement sheet — closed by D3. The sheet is skipped entirely: all 82 of its labels are marked SKIP in LEGACY_LABELS.csv (see Annex 2).
Reference syntax for live numbers. Section 10.2 is a sketch. It does not yet say how a reference names several qualifiers, or confirm that PL420 is shorthand for POVLINE_PL420. Since D13, a series_id such as POV_HC.POVLINE_PL420.PPP_2021 names a series unambiguously and is the natural reference key; the syntax is settled at the dashboard switch-over.
A model-based value that also fails the reliability rule. One row carries one status code, and E takes precedence over U (D22), so the reliability flag is lost on such a row and only the standard error shows it. If nowcasts with small-cell uncertainty become common, a separate reliability attribute may be warranted.
Series ids as SDMX code ids, closed by D43. Series ids contain ., and the SDMX IDType pattern for code ids allows only letters, digits, _, -, @ and $. The data lead chose on 2026-09-29 to keep the dotted ids unchanged in the data files: SERIES_ID is an uncoded mandatory String attribute, no codelist is derived from SERIES_PLAN.csv, and the project validator checks every value against that file (Section 6.1).

title: Appendix B. The data transition
text:
In September 2026 the dashboard’s inputs were converted, without changing a single number, into the files defined by the data standard. This page summarises what was done, which part was done by code and which by hand, and where each piece lives.

In one paragraph
The dashboard used to read two Excel workbooks in which every row is identified by a free-text label and every column by a spelled-out region name. The transition kept those files untouched in data_raw/, wrote down by hand how each label and column maps to a coded indicator, breakdown and area, and used R code to turn that mapping into a documented, machine-checkable dataset: one long table per country and year, plus codelists, boundaries, text and figures. What was done by hand
These are the judgement calls. Everything else is derived from them by code.

The mapping of the workbooks. pipeline/bootstrap/seeds/ holds seven small tables written during the transition:

label_triage.csv: each of the 179 workbook labels, what it measures, and whether to keep, skip, or treat as a duplicate or derivable series;
codes.csv: the codes and hierarchies of every codelist (breakdowns, qualifiers, units…);
geo_codes.csv: the 35 regions and zones, with the workbook column each one came from;
legacy_national_columns.csv: what each column of the National sheet means (urban/rural, sex of head, quintile…);
tab_plan.csv: which breakdowns are published for which geography;
legacy_overrides.csv: the 12 cells or columns withheld or flagged as wrong;
csv_headers.csv: the columns of every metadata file.

The definitions. pipeline/bootstrap/text/ holds the names, definitions, universes and notes of every indicator, breakdown, area, survey and figure (about 250 entries).
The standard itself. data-standard.qmd was revised to v0.4 to close 27 gaps found while writing the mapping, and to v0.5 after the acceptance (see below).
The decisions. The team settled the questions the data could not answer (see below).



What was done by code
All code is in R, under pipeline/. Every script runs from the repository root with --root ., and running it twice gives identical files.

Shared functions are in pipeline/R/, and unit tests in pipeline/tests/.
The bootstrap scripts (step 2) are now frozen. From metadata version 0.1.0 onward the metadata CSV files themselves are the source of truth, and they are edited directly. The seeds and bootstrap scripts are kept as the record of how the first version was built. Later structural changes are made by one-off scripts under pipeline/migrations/<version>/; the first, 0.2.0/migrate.R, took the metadata from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0 (below).


Main decisions

Inputs are never edited. Every fix goes into the mapping or the code, so the original workbooks remain the audit trail.
SEN Departement sheet skipped. It is an older version whose poverty totals disagree with ADM 1.
Known-bad values withheld, not corrected. The GNB Capital column (a copy of a zone) and 7 GNB cultivated-area outliers (up to 148 million ha) are left out and registered in LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv.
Empty cells kept as empty. They are recorded as “no value available” (OBS_STATUS = O) with a comment, never filled.
Three kinds of population share. A share of individuals, of households and of household enterprises get separate codes, because each needs its own weight.
GNB survey dated 2021. EHCVM 2021/22 is recorded as 2021.
Key messages taken from the dashboard. The version hard-coded in index.qmd was preferred over Messages_<ISO3>.txt.
19 ambiguous indicators coded as recommended. Examples: non-food share derived from the food share; three electricity indicators kept but flagged; household-head age groups kept as draft codes. All 19 were confirmed by the team and remain DRAFT.



Results

Senegal: 3,003 values (91 series × 33 population groups).
Guinea-Bissau: 2,268 values; 98 withheld as known errors; 39 empty in the source.
Coverage: every one of the 5,723 source cells is accounted for exactly once: converted, derived, duplicated, withheld or skipped.
Dictionary: 62 indicators, 13 breakdown variables (60 groups), 6 qualifiers (42 values), 35 geographic units in 6 schemes.
Checks: the validator finds no errors; the independent reconciliation matches every value.
Poverty headcounts reproduced exactly: SEN 3.13M / 6.52M and GNB 0.70M / 1.09M poor at $3.00 / $4.20 (2021 PPP).



What is still open

The dashboard still reads data_raw/. Pointing it at data/, metadata/, geo/ and content/ is the next step. (Done in the SDMX transition, below.)
Everything is DRAFT. Codes become ACTIVE only once the team confirms them.
The workbooks carry no sample sizes, population counts or standard errors. Producer files with those columns should replace them.
Some questions in the standard remain open: quintile definition, who owns metadata/, and the policy on boundary versions. How to record an indicator a country cannot produce was settled in v0.5 (a country row in SERIES_PLAN.csv).



After acceptance: standard v0.5 and metadata 0.2.0
On 2026-09-28 the standard was reviewed against the SDMX information model and revised to v0.5, with the metadata migrated to 0.2.0 and the data files regenerated. The review found the model sound and closed three kinds of gap: a data row could not be read from its key and the DSD alone, unit and provenance metadata sat at the file level rather than the row, and the population count on share rows was defined twice. In short:

Every data row now carries SERIES_ID, UNIT_MEASURE, PRECISION and SOURCE_ID, and the key gains an ESTIMATION dimension (SURVEY or MODEL), so a nowcast and a survey estimate for the same year can coexist. Files are named AFW360_HH_<ISO3>_<YEAR>_<ESTIMATION>.csv.
Verification rules and the indicator–qualifier relations moved out of codelist cells into metadata/rules/RULES.csv, metadata/structure/INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv and QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv; program runs are registered in metadata/registries/SOURCES.csv.
OBS_STATUS gains a rule-based low-reliability code and a definition-differs code; SERIES_PLAN.csv gains display names and per-country status.
Every table in the standard that lists a metadata file is generated from it and checked for staleness.

The decisions are recorded as D12 to D26 in the standard’s “Changes since v0.4” table. The values in data/ are unchanged: projecting the new files onto the old 26 columns reproduces the accepted files exactly, and the reconciliation still matches every cell.


How the work was run
The transition was carried out by AI agents in 17 work packages, each checked by an independent verifier, with the team deciding at three gates (hard cases, the standard, final acceptance on 2026-09-23). The detailed plan, the per-package instructions and the verification reports were removed once the work was accepted. They remain in the git history at commit af378e9, under .docs/transition/.


SDMX transition (standard v0.6, metadata 0.3.0)
On 2026-09-29 the files themselves were made SDMX 3.1 conformant, with the standard revised to v0.6 and the metadata migrated to 0.3.0 by pipeline/migrations/0.3.0/migrate.R. v0.5 already followed the SDMX information model in spirit; v0.6 makes the published files readable by SDMX tools while keeping CSV as the working format and the CSVs under metadata/, content/ and data/ as the source of truth. The same step switched the dashboard from data_raw/ to the harmonised files. In short:

Data. The two data files are SDMX-CSV 2.1 data messages: three fixed leading columns, one column per component of the data structure, 37 columns with a 19-column key, a FREQ dimension first, ACTION R on every row, and NaN where a value is intentionally missing.
Structures. pipeline/build_sdmx.R generates one SDMX-ML 3.1 structure message, sdmx/structures/AFW360_structures.xml, with 32 maintainables: the agency scheme, 22 codelists, a concept scheme of 82 concepts, the data structure and dataflow, the metadata structure and metadataflow, the data and metadata provider schemes and the two provision agreements. Agency WB.AFW360 is declared as a sub-agency of the World Bank’s WB. The file is validated against the vendored SDMX-ML 3.1.0 schemas before it is written.
Reference metadata. Surveys, sources, dashboard text and figures are published as four SDMX-CSV 2.1 metadata messages under sdmx/metadata/, generated from the registry CSVs.
Round trip. pipeline/import_sdmx.R turns a structure message (SDMX-ML 3.0 or 3.1) back into the metadata CSVs. Importing the generated message and rebuilding gives the same file byte for byte.
Checks. The validator gains six SDMX.* checks (staleness, schema, references, identity, data-file header, skipped). tools/verify/ checks the same files independently with pysdmx and lxml.
Dashboard. afw360/loader.py is the single data-access layer; the Senegal and Guinea-Bissau sections and the About page read data/, metadata/, content/, geo/ and assets/ through it. Guinea-Bissau now shows its own data, and every cell follows its indicator’s display rule.
Fusion Metadata Registry. FMR 12.4.2 was installed locally under tools/fmr/runtime/ (Tomcat 10.1, MySQL 8.0, no Docker, no administrator rights). It rejects SDMX-ML 3.1, so build_sdmx.R --sdmx-ml-version 3.0 writes a 3.0 profile without the metadata structure, metadataflow and metadata agreement. FMR loads that profile once the WB agency is registered, validates both SDMX-CSV 2.1 data files unchanged, and exports SDMX-ML 3.0, which the importer reads back with an empty diff. The workflow is in the FMR guide.

The decisions are recorded as D27 to D46 in the standard’s “Changes since v0.5” table and in metadata/CHANGELOG.md; the SDMX conformance page gives the evidence for each requirement. The main ones: target the SDMX 3.1 family (SDMX-CSV 2.1 for data and reference metadata, SDMX-ML 3.1 for structures, no SDMX-JSON); keep the pipeline in R, with Python only in the dashboard loader and the verification tool; align project codes to global SDMX, SDG and World Bank codelists where one exists; nine measures; registries become codelists plus metadatasets; SERIES_ID stays an uncoded attribute, because series ids contain dots.
The results: every value in data/ is unchanged (the reconciliation matches all 6871 cells, and projecting the new files onto the v0.5 columns reproduces them); the validator reports no errors; the test suite holds 1503 expectations; the SDMX files and the generated tables of the standard are current; the independent reader reports no failures.
What remains open: every code is still DRAFT; FMR cannot read the 3.1 message or the metadata structure, so the reference metadata files are checked only by the build, the validator and tools/verify; the page is not yet laid out as a Quarto dashboard.
The work was run as 30 work packages and three gates, all on 2026-09-29, on branch standard/v0.6-sdmx. An orchestrating agent wrote a brief for each package; Opus agents implemented them and fresh Sonnet agents verified each one against its own checklist before it was committed. The data lead decided at Gate 1 (the design, decisions D38 to D46), Gate 2 (install FMR now rather than defer) and Gate 3 (final acceptance and merge). The plan, the progress log with every commit hash and the surfaced points are in .docs/sdmx-transition/.

text:
Install steps (as run)
Commands run from the repository root; Git Bash unless marked PowerShell.

Check resources: free disk space, RAM and ports (netstat -ano | findstr LISTENING). Port 8005, Tomcat’s default shutdown port, was taken by a system process, so the shutdown port is 8015.
Download into tools/fmr/runtime/dl/ (curl needs --ssl-no-revoke on this machine):
curl --ssl-no-revoke -sSLO https://dlcdn.apache.org/tomcat/tomcat-10/v10.1.60/bin/apache-tomcat-10.1.60.zip
curl --ssl-no-revoke -sSLO https://github.com/bis-med-it/fmr-public/releases/download/v12.4.2/fmr-12.4.2.war
curl --ssl-no-revoke -sSLO https://dev.mysql.com/get/Downloads/MySQL-8.0/mysql-8.0.46-winx64.zip
curl --ssl-no-revoke -sSLO https://dev.mysql.com/get/Downloads/Connector-J/mysql-connector-j-9.6.0.zip
Check the Tomcat zip against its .sha512 file on downloads.apache.org, the WAR size against the GitHub release (129,151,617 bytes), and the MySQL zip’s MD5 against the MySQL download page.
Unzip (PowerShell Expand-Archive) to tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat and tools/fmr/runtime/mysql; copy the Connector/J jar to tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat/lib/ (Tomcat’s own lib, because the database connection is a Tomcat JNDI resource).
MySQL: write tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/my.ini:
[mysqld]
basedir=<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/mysql
datadir=<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/data
port=3306
bind-address=127.0.0.1
mysqlx=OFF
log-error=<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/logs/mysqld.err

port=3306
host=127.0.0.1
then initialise the data directory, start the server (see below) and create the database:
tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/bin/mysqld --defaults-file=tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/my.ini --initialize-insecure
tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/bin/mysql --defaults-file=tools/fmr/runtime/mysql/my.ini -u root -e \
  "CREATE DATABASE fmr CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;
   CREATE USER 'fmruser'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '<password>';
   GRANT ALL ON fmr.* TO 'fmruser'@'localhost'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;"
Tomcat configuration:

conf/server.xml: <Server port="8015" shutdown="SHUTDOWN">.
conf/context.xml: add, inside <Context>, the JNDI resource from the FMR wiki’s Jndi page:
<Resource name="fmrdatabase" auth="Container" type="javax.sql.DataSource"
  driverClassName="com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"
  url="jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/fmr?allowPublicKeyRetrieval=true&useSSL=false"
  username="fmruser" password="<password>"
  maxTotal="10" minIdle="5" maxWaitMillis="-1"
  timeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis="7200000" minEvictableIdleTimeMillis="3600000"
  defaultAutoCommit="false" />
bin/setenv.bat:
set "JAVA_OPTS=%JAVA_OPTS% -Xmx16g -Duser.home=<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/home -DRegistryProperties=file:///<repo>/tools/fmr/runtime/home/fmr.properties"
Copy fmr-12.4.2.war to webapps/ROOT.war and delete the default webapps/ROOT folder, so FMR is served at http://localhost:8080/.

Start Tomcat (see below). The first start takes about two minutes while the WAR unpacks; http://localhost:8080/ then redirects to /install.html.
First-run setup. In a browser: open http://localhost:8080/, accept the licence, choose JNDI connection with JNDI name fmrdatabase, context java:/comp/env, driver com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver, server URL http://localhost:8080, superuser root and a password. The same steps without a browser (the calls the setup page makes; a session cookie from install.html is required, otherwise the calls return 401):
B=http://localhost:8080/ws/secure/settings
C="-s -c tmp/fmr/cj -b tmp/fmr/cj -H Content-Type:application/json"
curl $C -o /dev/null http://localhost:8080/install.html
curl $C -X POST $B/saveLicenceAgreement
curl $C -d '{"jndiName":"fmrdatabase","jndiContext":"java:/comp/env","driver":"com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"}' $B/saveDatabaseSettings
curl $C -d 'http://localhost:8080' $B/saveServerUrl
curl $C -d 'Fusion Metadata Registry' $B/saveRegistryName
curl $C -d '{"username":"root","password":"<password>","maxLoginAttempts":"-1"}' $B/saveRootSecuritySettings
curl $C -X POST $B/completeInstall
Each call returns {"Success":[true]}. Afterwards http://localhost:8080/ returns 200 and the fmr database holds 34 tables.

title: FMR guide: local Fusion Metadata Registry for the AFW 360 standard
text:
Workflow
All commands run from the repository root in Git Bash, with FMR started (see Start and stop). The scripts use the R packages curl and jsonlite. The FMR address comes from FMR_BASE (default http://localhost:8080); the account used to load structures comes from FMR_USER and FMR_PASSWORD, or else from tools/fmr/runtime/secrets.txt (FMR_ADMIN_USER, FMR_ADMIN_PASSWORD). Every response is kept under tmp/fmr/.

1. Generate the SDMX files
Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root .
This writes the canonical SDMX-ML 3.1 message under sdmx/. It is not what FMR loads (see the status box); step 2 builds the 3.0 profile itself.


2. Load the structures
Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_load.R --root .
The script runs four steps:

FMR up? GET <FMR_BASE>/ must return 200.
Register the agency WB, once. The structure message declares the sub-agency WB.AFW360 in the agency scheme WB:AGENCIES(1.0). FMR can only store that scheme when the top-level agency WB exists in its own scheme SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0); otherwise the load fails with
HTTP 404, error code 100: Could not resolve reference from structure
Agency Scheme 'WB:AGENCIES(1.0)' to structure Agency
'urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.base.Agency=SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0).WB'
The script reads GET /sdmx/v2/structure/agencyscheme/SDMX/AGENCIES/1.0 and, only when WB is missing, submits tools/fmr/agencies_bootstrap.xml (a SDMX-ML 3.0 message holding SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0) with the items SDMX and WB) to the same endpoint as step 4. The FMR superuser account from the install has the rights for this; no UI step is needed. On a fresh FMR the scheme holds only SDMX, which the bootstrap keeps. Response saved to tmp/fmr/agencies_response.xml. In the web interface the same is done under Agencies by adding WB to the top-level scheme.
Build the SDMX-ML 3.0 profile:
Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root . --sdmx-ml-version 3.0 --out-root tmp/fmr/v30
writes tmp/fmr/v30/sdmx/structures/AFW360_structures.xml: the 22 codelists, concept scheme, data structure, dataflow, provision agreement and agency and provider schemes with v3_0 namespaces; no metadata structure, metadataflow or metadata provision agreement (their 3.0 XML differs).
Load it: POST /ws/secure/sdmxapi/rest/ with the file as the application/xml body, header ACTION: REPLACE (option --action) and HTTP Basic authentication. The response is saved to tmp/fmr/load_response.xml. The script exits 0 on HTTP 200 and prints Success when FMR reports stored structures. A repeated load of an unchanged message returns HTTP 200 with an empty SubmitStructureResponse (nothing to replace), printed as HTTP 200.

Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_load.R --root . --file <message.xml> skips steps 2 and 3 and loads the given message. The same load is possible in the web interface (Load Structures), with the 3.0 profile.


3. Validate the data
Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_validate.R --root .
Each data/AFW360_HH_*_SURVEY.csv is POSTed unchanged to POST /ws/public/data/validate (no login needed) with Content-Type: application/vnd.sdmx.data+csv;version=2.1.0. FMR answers with a JSON report, saved as tmp/fmr/<ISO3>_<YEAR>_SURVEY_validation.json. The script prints one line per file and exits 0 only when every report says "Errors": false and lists no error entries. Result on 2026-09-29:
AFW360_HH_GNB_2021_SURVEY.csv: HTTP 200, format SDMX CSV v2.0, dataflow WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0), 2268 observations, Errors: false, error entries: 0
AFW360_HH_SEN_2021_SURVEY.csv: HTTP 200, format SDMX CSV v2.0, dataflow WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0), 3003 observations, Errors: false, error entries: 0
FMR reads the SDMX-CSV 2.1 files as it reads SDMX-CSV 2.0 (the report’s FileFormat says SDMX CSV v2.0): the header STRUCTURE,STRUCTURE_ID,ACTION,... is the same in both versions and the files use no 2.1-only feature. The data files need no change.


4. Export and round trip
Rscript tools/fmr/fmr_export.R --root . --out tmp/fmr/export.xml
Rscript pipeline/import_sdmx.R --root . --diff tmp/fmr/export.xml
fmr_export.R GETs /sdmx/v2/structure/*/WB,WB.AFW360/*/*?detail=full, every artefact maintained by WB (the scheme WB:AGENCIES) or WB.AFW360. It asks for SDMX-ML 3.1 first; FMR 12.4.2 answers HTTP 406, so the script takes SDMX-ML 3.0 (v3_0 namespaces), which import_sdmx.R reads. With the structures loaded as in step 2, the diff prints nothing on standard output: FMR returns every code, name, description and annotation that the CSVs under metadata/ hold. import_sdmx.R notes on standard error that CL_FIGURE, CL_SOURCE and CL_SURVEY are derived from registries and are reported, not written; that is expected. What does not travel: the metadata structure, metadataflow and metadata provision agreement (not in the 3.0 profile, so not in FMR), and the message header (FMR writes its own ID and sender).


5. Edit structures in FMR
In FMR, work on a copy versioned <next>-draft; export it (step 4); run Rscript pipeline/import_sdmx.R --root . --diff <export.xml> to see the changes against the CSVs, then --apply; commit through a pull request; at release, bump metadata/VERSION, regenerate (step 1) and reload (step 2).


6. Validation-only use
Steps 1 to 3.

title: FMR guide: local Fusion Metadata Registry for the AFW 360 standard
text:
Findings from the install

FMR 12.4.2 runs on Azul Zulu 21 (not named as tested by the vendor) and Tomcat 10.1.60 with MySQL 8.0.46 and Connector/J 9.6.0.
FMR rejects SDMX-ML 3.1 structure messages (error 150, status box) and does not offer 3.1 on export (HTTP 406); it loads and exports SDMX-ML 3.0.
FMR needs the top-level agency WB in SDMX:AGENCIES(1.0) before any WB.AFW360 structure loads; fmr_load.R registers it when missing.
FMR accepts the SDMX-CSV 2.1 data files as they are and reports them as SDMX-CSV 2.0.
FMR’s error and submission responses are SDMX-ML 2.1 documents, whatever the version of the message sent.
FMR’s default home folder is <user home>\SDMX_IO\FMR; with -Duser.home and -DRegistryProperties set as above, the only file it writes there, the generated fmr.properties, lands in tools/fmr/runtime/home/, and no SDMX_IO folder appears in the user profile. FMR’s own logs go to tools/fmr/runtime/tomcat/logs/.
The setup page’s calls need a session cookie from install.html; without it they return HTTP 401.
